title: Arathi Highlands
body: The Arathi Highlands are a country of rolling green hills and scattered pines, and the birthplace of the first human nation. Here Thoradin united the human tribes into the Empire of Arathor and raised Strom, its first capital, with a great wall to hold back the Amani trolls. The Trollbane kings who later ruled Stromgarde from the old capital warred with the Witherbark trolls for generations. Those days are gone. King Thoras Trollbane is dead and his city lies in ruins, carved up between Prince Galen's militia, the outlaws of the Syndicate and the Boulderfist ogres. The last soldiers of Stromgarde hold Refuge Pointe in the heart of the highlands, while in the northeast the Horde has rebuilt Hammerfall on the site of an old orc internment camp. Witherbark warbands and ogres press them all. Beneath the hills, a voice calls out through glowing crystals, begging to be set free, and on the southern coast a pirate crew sits marooned in Faldir's Cove.

title: Thoradin's Wall
body: From the highlands, Thoradin's Wall marks the western edge of the land, a long line of weathered stone between Arathi and the foothills beyond. King Thoradin raised it to guard Strom, the first human capital, and the ruins of that city, now called Stromgarde, still lie near it. The wall has held no army back for a very long time. Highland striders hunt along its foot and plains creepers crawl among its fallen stones. Where Thoradin once feared troll warbands, the highlands now face ogres, outlaws and the Witherbark all at once, and the old barrier stops none of them.

title: Northfold Manor
body: Northfold Manor is a farm estate on the northwestern edge of the highlands. After Stromgarde fell, the Syndicate seized it as an outpost, and highwaymen, mercenaries and pathstalkers now hold its fields and barns. From here the outlaws command the country between Refuge Pointe and Southshore, so that the supplies the Stromgarde defenders need from Hillsbrad rarely get through. Worse things have happened here than banditry. The shaman Tor'gan of Hammerfall traced a burning unease in his blood to the manor and found the traces of demonic summoning, with a spent bloodstone amulet lying on the ground. A rarely seen outlaw called Singer lurks in the small house.

title: Boulder'gor
body: Boulder'gor is an ogre mound in the western highlands, northeast of the ruins of Stromgarde. Boulderfist ogres and enforcers crowd its camps, and Witherbark trolls come and go among them, a sign of the pact the two peoples have made against their common enemies. A brutish ogre named Kovork is sometimes found there. For the Horde, the mound serves as a proving ground: Tallow of Tarren Mill sends would-be recruits here to test their strength before they are trusted to join the defenders of Hammerfall.

title: The Circles of Binding
body: Four rings of standing stones lie scattered across the highlands: the Circles of West, East and Outer Binding, and the strongest of them, the Circle of Inner Binding, close to the ruins of Stromgarde. Each holds a Stone of Binding, and together they pin something deep beneath the earth. Elemental exiles keep watch over them: creatures of flame at the western circle, of water in the east, of thunder at the outer ring and of rumbling stone at the inner one, where a Keystone stands among the stones as a final lock. Near the eastern circle walks Fozruk, a stone watcher who carries the key to that lock, attended by a small band of kobolds.

title: Stromgarde Keep
body: Once Strom, the first capital of humankind, Stromgarde was long the seat of the Trollbane kings. Now it is a ruin and a battlefield. Prince Galen Trollbane's militia holds the quarter around the chapel and the Sanctum behind it, where King Thoras lies entombed with the sword Trol'kalar. The Syndicate under Lord Falconcrest commands the inner keep, while the Boulderfist ogres, Witherbark berserkers at their side, have taken the old mage district and the Tower of Arathor, whose master, Archmage Trelane, tried to hold it and failed. None of the three can drive out the others, and the bloody stalemate grinds on while the defenders dwindle.

title: Faldir's Cove
body: On the rugged southern coast lies Faldir's Cove, named, it seems, for Faldir, the descendant of Thoradin who led his followers away from Arathor to found the kingdom of Stormwind. Today it shelters the Harbinger, the one ship of Captain Shakes O'Breen's Blackwater Raiders to come in safely. The pirates sailed from Booty Bay after a lost elven treasure, but as the other two ships followed the Harbinger in, the sea rumbled, the tide fell away and both were wrecked on the reef. The survivors now camp beside the water with a pair of gnomish inventors, unable to leave until the tide rises and the naga stop watching.

title: The Drowned Reef
body: Off the coast southwest of Faldir's Cove lies the Drowned Reef, and it is not only a reef. Sunken stonework, something like a temple, lies beneath the waves, guarded by the Daggerspine naga, and it is said the strange tide that wrecked the Blackwater Raiders was their doing. The Maiden's Folly and the Spirit of Silverpine ran aground on it and sank so fast that few escaped, and the naga slew the survivors in the water. The ships' logs and charts still lie in the wrecks, and gems from an old elven treasure, calcified into stone, are scattered across the sea floor. A naga called Prince Nazjak hunts these waters.

title: Refuge Pointe
body: Refuge Pointe, in the heart of the highlands, is the last stronghold of the kingdom of Stromgarde. When the city fell, the remnants of its army refused to abandon the land and withdrew here, and under Captain Nials they have sworn not to leave until the king's banner flies over Stromgarde once more. It is a spare camp of tents, a forge, a few merchants and a gryphon roost, ringed by defenders, and its wanted board posts the militia's bounties on Syndicate leaders. Two agents of Archmage Malin of Stormwind, the dwarf Skuerto and Apprentice Kryten, have also made camp here, sent to recover what Archmage Trelane left behind when the city fell.

title: Dabyrie's Farmstead
body: In the north of the highlands stands Dabyrie's Farmstead, home of a family that still holds to the kingdom of Stromgarde. Kenata Dabyrie keeps the farm with her children Fardel and Marcel, and a crew of laborers works the fields under the protection of the Dabyrie Militia. Not everyone is glad that they prospered. In the Undercity, the Forsaken Genavie Callow, who lost her family to the plague and saw her estate looted and burned in the war, swears the Dabyries stole the last precious things she owned, and she wants all of their heads for it.

title: Go'Shek Farm
body: Go'Shek Farm, in the east of the highlands, has been taken over by the Horde to help feed Hammerfall, and peons work its fields under the watch of grunts. Not all of its business is farming. Forsaken bodyguards stand over a small house to the south, where Apothecary Jorell works in secret and promises anyone who troubles him that he will find a use for their body once they are dead. Couriers slip away from the house toward Tarren Mill, and the farm has drawn quiet watchers from Southshore who suspect the Forsaken are brewing something terrible.

title: Hammerfall
body: Hammerfall stands in the northeast of the highlands on ground the orcs remember with bitterness. After the Second War this was one of the largest of the human internment camps, where captured orcs were held behind wood and steel. Thrall and Orgrim Doomhammer stormed it to free the prisoners, and in that battle a knight charged Doomhammer from behind and ran him through with his lance, a mortal wound. When the Horde returned to the highlands, it raised an outpost on the ruins and named it in the fallen warchief's honor. Now Drum Fel leads its defense against the Boulderfist ogres and Witherbark trolls, who have joined forces to drive the Horde out.

title: Drywhisker Gorge
body: Drywhisker Gorge cuts into the hills east of Hammerfall and ends in a cave held by the Drywhisker kobolds. They are allies of the giants who keep a prisoner beneath Arathi, and they carry motes of that prisoner's power. Nearby, a cluster of iridescent shards juts from the rock, much like the Shards of Myzrael, though it lacks their reassuring warmth. The gorge is also the only known source of lesser bloodstone ore, and the kobold geomancer Flintdagger is sometimes seen among the diggers and surveyors.

title: Witherbark Village
body: In the southeast of the highlands, around a small lake, lies Witherbark Village, home of the forest trolls who have been sworn enemies of Stromgarde for generations. Axe throwers, headhunters and witch doctors fill the huts, while the shadow hunters, the strongest of whom carry a special knife earned in their rites of passage, keep to a large cavern behind the village where the tribe's leaders are often found, among them the warband leader Zalas Witherbark. A second warband leader, Nimar the Slayer, also stalks the village. The Witherbark have made common cause with the Boulderfist ogres, and together they have set out to drive the Horde from Hammerfall.

title: Boulderfist Hall
body: Boulderfist Hall is an ogre stronghold in the south of the highlands, east of the Thandol Span. Brutes and magi of the Boulderfist clan hold it, and the defenders of Hammerfall count them a harder foe than the Witherbark. A hulking ogre known as Molok the Crusher is sometimes found there. Of late, one of the hall's ogres, Kor'gresh Coldrage, has been hurling blasts of ice at his own kin to keep them in line, using a wand that once belonged to Archmage Trelane of Stromgarde.

title: Thandol Span
body: The Thandol Span comes to ground at the southern tip of the highlands, and the Arathi end of the crossing is no safer than the Wetlands side. Dark Iron shadowcasters, bombardiers and suppliers have made camp on the slopes just beyond the bridge. Out on the span, the dwarf sentry Foggy MacKreel nurses a sore head. He drank too much moonshine and slept through his watch, and recalls only a rumbling overhead, as if a whole brigade of siege engines had rolled past. He fears Longbraid would have his head if he knew, and frets about a moonshine debt he owes a brewmeister in Southshore.

title: Captain Nials
body: Captain Nials commands the remnants of the Stromgarde army at Refuge Pointe. Her city has fallen, and honor and duty bind her soldiers to the highlands until the king's banner flies over Stromgarde once more, so firmly that she turned away the dwarves of the Wetlands when they asked for aid. She knows the war is going badly, her ranks thinning while the enemy grows. When the badges of her fallen soldiers are taken back from the Syndicate, she reads their names aloud one by one and sighs that so many have been lost, and so many more must be before the battle ends. Then she sends word to their families.

title: Prince Galen Trollbane
body: Galen Trollbane is the son of King Thoras Trollbane and heir to a kingdom in ruins. With his father dead, he leads the militia that holds part of Stromgarde, keeping to a chapel deep in the city beside the Sanctum where Thoras lies entombed with the ancestral sword Trol'kalar. To guard the tomb, the sigils that unseal it were divided among the survivors: the sigil of Thoradin Galen broke into five pieces and gave to his defenders, the sigil of Arathor went to his cavalry leader Valorcall, and the sigil of Trollbane he keeps on his own person. He is well guarded and a capable warrior in his own right.

title: Lord Falconcrest and Otto
body: The Syndicate is a brotherhood of outlaws led by nobles of fallen Alterac, and in the Arathi Highlands its efforts are directed by Lord Falconcrest from the ruins of Stromgarde. His outlaws hold the inner keep, and the Syndicate's leaders pay their rabble gold for every badge taken from a dead Stromgarde soldier. At Falconcrest's side stands his bodyguard Otto, no strategist but a fierce fighter who has killed dozens of the city's defenders, and who assures his master that everything is going as planned. The Stromgarde militia has put a price on both their heads.

title: Marez Cowl
body: Marez Cowl is a warlock and a high-ranking advisor and operative of the Syndicate, last seen in the outlaw-held quarter of Stromgarde. She traffics openly with demons. With a bloodstone orb she has called them forth in great numbers, a power the shaman Tor'gan of Hammerfall feels as a burning in his own blood. Captain Nials has heard it whispered that Marez is an emissary between the Syndicate and some other, darker power. Refuge Pointe and Hammerfall agree on little, but both want her dead.

title: Drum Fel and Korin Fel
body: Drum Fel leads the defense of Hammerfall, a hard warrior with little patience for the untested and no time even to sharpen his axe. He sends every able fighter against the Witherbark and Boulderfist warbands that besiege the outpost, praising courage and scorning cowardice in equal measure, and believes Hammerfall will thrive in the highlands once its enemies are broken. His wife, Korin Fel, is a seer who loves him enough to deceive him. Her auguries revealed that the ogre Or'Kalar has laid a trap for her husband, and she has hidden every sign of the ogre from Drum, knowing he would rush off to face his old foe.

title: Gor'mul
body: Gor'mul is an orc warrior of the old Horde who was once a prisoner in the internment camp that stood where Hammerfall is now. He saw Orgrim Doomhammer come in his midnight plate to free the camp, and saw a knight on horseback run the Warchief through from behind. As the earth shook and the other prisoners escaped, Gor'mul was left behind, and he wandered alone and without hope for years until the Horde returned. Bitter that he was not allowed to die beside his Warchief, he scorned every charm brought to cheer him, until the shaman Tor'gan let him feel the guile of the raptor and the strength the shamans had found again.

title: Tor'gan
body: Tor'gan is a troll shaman of Hammerfall, a practitioner of the shamanic magic the Horde has found anew under its young Warchief Thrall. He has spent much patience on Gor'mul, crafting amulets and orbs filled with the spirit of the raptor in the hope of waking the warrior within. He feels fouler magic too. A burning in his blood led him to Northfold Manor and the traces of demonic summoning there, and to the warlock in Stromgarde whose bloodstone orb he vowed to destroy. When the five shattered pieces of the sigil of Thoradin were laid before him, he bound them whole again, and found it easier than he expected.

title: Or'Kalar
body: Or'Kalar is a Boulderfist ogre who leads his clan's forces in Stromgarde, a pawn of Mug'thol, and he lurks near the Tower of Arathor. Years ago he was beaten by Drum Fel of Hammerfall, and he has hated him ever since. The attacks on Hammerfall are part of his design, a trap meant to draw Drum Fel out to his death. Only Drum's wife Korin knows it. She saw the plot in her auguries and hid all signs of the ogre from her husband, quietly seeking someone else to end the threat.

title: Myzrael
body: Myzrael calls herself a princess of the earth, held captive deep beneath the Arathi Highlands by the giants. Her only voice in the world above comes through crystal shards that break the surface in the northern hills, and through them she pleads for rescue, stirring a feeling of warmth and safety in all who listen. Those who set her free learn too late what she is. Summoned before her strength has returned, she turns on her rescuer and names them a fool for helping her. She has other servants already: cultists of the Twilight's Hammer revere her as their Lady and know how she may be called to the surface.

title: Shakes O'Breen
body: Captain Shakes O'Breen of the Blackwater Raiders led three ships out of Booty Bay to Faldir's Cove, steered by one of Professor Phizzlethorpe's contraptions toward a lost elven treasure. Only his own ship, the Harbinger, came through. He dreads what Fleet Master Seahorn will say about the loss, though Seahorn calls him the right captain for the job. O'Breen does not value his own life above his crew's, but he knows they cannot reach home without his knowledge of the seas, so when the naga gather for an attack he stands on the high ground beside the cannon to drive them back.

title: The Defenders of Stromgarde
body: From Refuge Pointe, Captain Nials fights a war she is losing. Her soldiers, the Syndicate and the ogres have divided Stromgarde in a bloody stalemate, and while her ranks thin, the enemy's swell. Help must come from Southshore, but the Syndicate holds the land between, so the outlaws of Northfold Manor must be cleared before the supply trains can get through. Inside the city, Syndicate leaders pay their rabble gold for every badge cut from a fallen militiaman, and Nials wants each one returned, so that families may at least know their loved ones died in battle. The wanted board at Refuge Pointe names the true targets: Marez Cowl, a warlock rumored to deal with some darker power, and Lord Falconcrest and his bodyguard Otto, whose deaths would throw the Syndicate's efforts in the highlands into disarray.

title: Trelane's Treasures
body: When Stromgarde fell, Archmage Trelane tried and failed to hold the Tower of Arathor, then fled to Stormwind, leaving his belongings behind. His former apprentice, Archmage Malin, sent two agents to recover them: the gruff dwarf Skuerto and Apprentice Kryten, who set up camp at Refuge Pointe. While Kryten sought Witherbark reagents for Malin, Skuerto went scouting and came back from Boulderfist Hall looking as if he had tangled with the ogres, having learned that the ogre Kor'gresh Coldrage had taken Trelane's Wand of Invocation and was close to mastering it. With the wand recovered, the rest lay in the tower itself, now overrun by ogres. A gem the Boulderfist shaman had stolen from the tower, enchanted by Kryten and pressed to a pedestal at its foot, woke the tower's old defenses, and Trelane's phylactery, orb and ember agate were carried out of their chests and home to a delighted Malin.

title: Hammerfall Besieged
body: Hammerfall is under constant attack. In Tarren Mill, Tallow tests would-be defenders against the ogres of Boulder'gor before sending them to Drum Fel, who names the enemy plainly: the Witherbark trolls, who turned their backs on the Horde, and the Boulderfist ogres, who would make meat and bedding of orcs, have joined forces to drive Hammerfall from the land. Drum's champions carry the war to the Witherbark camps to the south, then to the brutes and magi of the ogre lair toward the dwarven bridge, and finally to the Boulderfist lords and shaman who direct the raids from the ruins of Stromgarde. Drum's wife Korin knows what he does not: the attacks are the work of Or'Kalar, an ogre who has hated her husband since Drum defeated him years ago and has laid a trap for him. Quietly, she asks for Or'Kalar's head instead.
sources: quests 676, 677, 678, 679, 680 (descriptions, completion and reward texts)

title: Trol'kalar
body: In the days of Arathor, Lord Ignaeus of Strom, called Trollbane, rode against the trolls with Trol'kalar, whose name means troll slayer, and for generations Strom and Arathor ravaged the trolls with it. With Thoras Trollbane dead and Stromgarde in ruins, Vol'jin resolved to take the sword for the Darkspear and turn it on the trolls of Zul'Gurub, and sent the hunter Zengu to Hammerfall to see it done. The blade lay sealed in Thoras's tomb behind wards only the sigils could break. The sigil of Strom was taken from the Syndicate, who had stolen it. The sigil of Thoradin, split into five among the city's defenders, was gathered and bound whole by Tor'gan. The sigil of Arathor was won from Lieutenant Valorcall, and the last from Prince Galen himself, slain in his chapel. Joined, they became the Sigil of Ignaeus, and at its touch the stone hands of the tomb released the sword, bound for Nimboya at Grom'gol.

title: The Princess Beneath the Stones
body: Those who touch the Shards of Myzrael in the northern hills hear a voice pleading for help: a princess of the earth, she says, imprisoned far below by the giants. To strengthen her, the Drywhisker kobolds are robbed of the motes of her power and a second cluster of shards in their gorge is woken. Next come the Stones of Binding. Keys taken from the circles of West, East and Outer Binding open the Stone of Inner Binding, and the Rod of Order, won from the stone watcher Fozruk, unlocks the Keystone. Myzrael cries out that she is free, and sends her rescuer to her servants in the Twilight's Hammer, who know how she may be called to the surface. That road leads to the Badlands and Theldurin the Lost, and in the end the summons is turned against her: called up at the Shards before her power is whole, Myzrael is defeated and bound again in her own Eldritch Shackles, and the shards pulse now with open menace.

title: The Blackwater Expedition
body: Shakes O'Breen's Blackwater Raiders came to Faldir's Cove expecting to stay only a few hours, just long enough to raise a lost elven treasure and sail home to Booty Bay. Instead the sea rumbled, the tide fell away and two of their three ships broke apart on the Drowned Reef. Now the crew needs help. First Mate Nilzlix wants the wrecks' logs and charts recovered before prying eyes find them, and Captain Steelgut, who lost his Maiden's Folly and woke on the shore after the naga slew his crew, wants the Daggerspine made to pay. The gnomes Phizzlethorpe and Draxlegauge charge a pair of goggles from a cursed rune stone in a cave up the hill, and through them the calcified elven gems on the sea floor shine plainly. When the naga mass for an attack, O'Breen holds the high ground with a cannon, then sends a sample gem to Fleet Master Seahorn as proof of the find.
